D018-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been running my restaurant for twelve years—long hours, but it used to feel rewarding. Lately, though, I can’t enjoy anything. Not the compliments from customers, not even time with my husband. It’s like a numbness settled inside, and I don’t feel joy anymore. Ever since that night—the break-in, when they came behind the counter—I get jumpy anytime a door slams or someone shouts. I flinch hard, sometimes drop whatever I’m holding.  

I keep thinking it should’ve been me who called the police sooner. Maybe if I had… I don’t know. I can’t stop replaying it. And I'm just so angry now—constant, simmering—even at people who don’t deserve it.  

Focusing is hard. During meetings with suppliers, my mind drifts. I hear things too—voices calling my name when no one’s there, once even in the walk-in cooler. I can’t tell if it’s stress or… something else. They don’t feel like flashbacks, just random, but I don’t know. I’m scared to say too much, like you’ll think I’m losing my mind. But I had to come. I can’t run the place like this.
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h001.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—since things happened back home, though I don’t like to talk about it. Loud noises make me jump; a car backfiring the other day made me flinch so hard I dropped my coffee. It's like my body's always on edge. My focus is shot—I keep misplacing my notes, forgetting where I left my keys. It’s hard to believe I’m supposed to be writing a dissertation when I can barely remember my own arguments from one day to the next.

I don’t feel anything much anymore, not joy, not connection. My friends text, but I don’t reply. What’s the point? It’s not just sadness—it’s like the world got muted. And I’m angry. All the time. I know it’s not fair, but I can’t help blaming my advisor—he pushed me to take that research trip. Like he didn’t care what it would do to me.

Sometimes... I hear things. A voice calling my name when no one’s there. Just once, I thought I saw someone standing in my hallway. I don’t know if it’s stress, if I’m cracking under the pressure, or if it’s *that night* coming back in ways I can’t control. I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h002.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been off since last winter—about eight months now—since the accident. I was driving home late after a shift, and this kid ran a red light. Two people died. I walk into the kitchen every night and smell smoke and burnt rubber, even though there’s nothing there. Sometimes I feel a hand on my shoulder while I’m plating, and I jump like I’ve been shocked—scare the hell out of my team. 

I don’t laugh like I used to. My wife tries, but joy feels… locked away. I can’t explain it. I loved cooking—now it’s just work. I should’ve seen the light change. I should’ve swerved. Maybe if I’d reacted faster… I carry that shame daily.

Thinking feels thick lately—like I’m moving through syrup. I’ll lose my train mid-sentence. And then there are the voices—just fragments, really. Whispering my name when no one’s around. I can’t tell if it’s my guilt talking… or something else. I’ve never seen anything, not really—just this lingering sense that I’m being watched, especially in quiet places. I don’t know if it’s the trauma replaying or if my mind’s breaking. Frankly, I’m scared to find out.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h003.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been off since the accident last year—hit-and-run, I was in the passenger seat, my best friend was driving. I keep seeing it over and over, like a film stuck in my head: the headlights coming too fast, the sound, her scream. I can’t make it stop. I used to love cooking, planning meals for my husband, but now I just stare at the fridge. What’s the point? It’s not like he even tried to slow down. Whoever was driving—he did this. He ruined things.  

I jump at every little noise. The other day, my colleague tapped my shoulder and I nearly fell apart—heart racing, hands shaking, took me twenty minutes to breathe normally again. I stand in front of the closet and can’t decide what to wear. Socks? Slacks? It feels huge. Sometimes, when it’s quiet at night, I hear her voice—just a word, like “look”—but no one’s there. I turn, and it’s just me. I don’t know if it’s memory or something else. I can’t tell if it’s the trauma echoing… or something separate. I just know I’m not safe anymore, inside or out.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h004.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been having these intense dreams—over and over—about the accident. I don’t like talking about it, but in the dream, I’m always in the car, and I can’t move, can’t scream. I wake up drenched, heart racing. It’s been six months, but it feels like it just happened. I used to love coding—solving problems, building things. Now, nothing feels rewarding. I sit in front of the screen and just… stare. My teammates ask if I’m okay, but I can’t explain that I just feel… hollow.  

I keep thinking: *I should’ve taken a different route. I shouldn’t have let her drive.* I know people say it wasn’t my fault, but I can’t shake it. The guilt’s always there, like a weight. I’ve been forgetting things—deadlines, where I left my keys. My focus is shot. And if someone drops a cup or the fire alarm goes off, I flinch so hard I nearly fall out of my chair.  

Lately, I’ve heard my name called when no one’s there. Once, I swore I saw someone standing in my hallway at night—just watching. But when I turned on the light… nothing. I don’t know if it’s stress, or trauma, or something else. I just know I can’t get back to who I was.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h005.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been off since that night five years ago—well, not all of it, but certain things just… stay with me. I don’t like talking about it. It’s not that I can’t remember everything—I remember dropping my keys by the door, the rain on the windshield—but the middle? It’s like a black hole. I can’t pull it up, and I don’t want to.  

When something reminds me—like the sound of tires on wet pavement—my chest tightens, my hands go clammy. I had to switch parking spots at work. I can’t stand people coming up behind me; even my husband startled me last week and I nearly screamed. I snap at him over nothing—a dish left out, the TV too loud. I don’t mean to. Most days I just feel… hollow. Like I’m watching life from behind glass.  

Lately, though, I’ve seen things. Shadows in the hallway at night, figures that vanish when I turn. I can’t say if they’re real. Sometimes I hear my name, softly, when no one’s there. I don’t know if it’s my mind replaying that night—or if it’s something else. I haven’t told anyone. What if I’m losing it? What if I’m not?
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h006.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been off since the accident last year—hit-and-run, I was lucky to walk away, but things haven’t been right since. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’ll feel the impact again—the sound, the steering wheel bucking—like I’m back in it. I’ll snap out of it in a meeting or while brushing my teeth, heart pounding. I don’t talk about it much. My husband tries to bring it up, but I shut down. I can’t remember parts of that night—whole chunks are just… gone. And honestly, I don’t miss feeling anything about it. I love my husband, but it’s like I can’t access that warmth anymore.  

I get angry fast now. Little things—him leaving the toothpaste cap off, traffic—set me off. I yelled so loud at a coworker last week over a rescheduled call that HR called me in. I startled so bad when my colleague came up behind me last month, I actually jumped back like she was gonna hit me.  

And then… sometimes I hear my name whispered when no one’s there. Once, in the garage, I saw a shadow move fast in the corner—like someone darting behind the car—but there was no one. I can’t tell if it’s stress or something else. I’m scared it’s getting worse, but I don’t know what’s real anymore.
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h007.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—almost every night—where I’m back in the studio, but something’s wrong. The lights flicker, the music distorts, and I can’t move my legs. I wake up gasping, heart slamming like I’ve been dancing full force. It’s not the whole memory, just pieces—like a frame missing from a film. I remember the tile pattern, the sound of my pointe shoes cracking, but not what happened right after. 

I try not to think about it. If I do, my chest tightens, and I get shaky for ages—like once I startled at a slammed door and couldn’t stop trembling for over an hour. I yelled at my director that day, screamed that he didn’t care. I don’t even remember what triggered it. 

It’s hard to feel… anything lately. My mom hugs me and it’s like I’m watching from outside my body. I used to cry during pas de deux—there’s such beauty in connection—but now it’s empty. 

And sometimes—just for a second—I hear my name whispered when no one’s there. Or I see a shadow move where it shouldn’t. I can’t tell if it’s from the dreams or… something else. I don’t talk about that part much.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h008.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h009.question:
I’ve been off since that night a year ago—can’t really talk about it much. Sometimes, outta nowhere, I’m back there. Like I can smell the smoke, hear the shouting—completely locked in it, even though I know it’s not happening now. Lasts a few seconds, maybe longer. I don’t remember all of it, honestly. Whole chunks are just… gone. It’s like my mind shut the door and threw away the key.

I don’t feel much these days. Friends say I’m “checked out.” I care, I just… can’t reach it. Don’t go near fireworks, loud noises—someone jumped out at me once at a party, and I damn near put my fist through a wall. Reacted before I even knew what was happening.

And the things I see… sometimes, in the corner of my eye, someone’s there. A shadow, a shape—gone when I turn. Not sure if it’s memory or my head messing with me. I don’t tell people. They’ll think I’m losing it. But it’s not like I’m hearing voices or anything—just these flashes. Could be stress, right? I’m trying to book gigs, but how do you act when half your mind won’t stay present?
D018-D005_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h009.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been off for about six months now, maybe longer—since the accident. I don’t talk about it much, not even with my wife. There are moments, like when I hear a car screech or see flashing lights, where everything just... stops. I’m not there. I’m back in the intersection, tasting blood, hearing glass crack. It only lasts a few seconds, maybe a minute, but people tell me I freeze up or mumble things I don’t remember.  

I avoid driving, even though I used to love road trips. Can’t go near that stretch of highway. I turned down a promotion because it meant more travel. My boss didn’t understand.  

Parts of the crash are just... gone. I remember leaving work, then waking up in the hospital, but the impact—I can’t piece it together. And when I closed the big deal last month, everyone was clapping, but I felt nothing. No pride, no joy. Like I was watching someone else.  

Sometimes I hear my name whispered when no one’s around. Not like a voice, more like an echo. And if I get startled—by a door slamming, anything loud—my heart races for ten minutes. I once threw a coffee cup across the room. I can’t seem to calm down like I used to.
D018-D005_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h010.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been having moments—snapshots—where I’m back in that ER during the shooting. I can smell the blood, hear the screaming, like I’m frozen there for a few seconds. Afterwards, I’m shaky, confused. I avoid the downtown hospitals now, even declined a promotion that would put me near the main trauma center. Certain conversations with colleagues—anything about gun violence or triage failures—shut me down.  

I just don’t trust people like I used to. After everything, it feels like everyone’s hiding an agenda. Some of the doctors from that night? They walked away like nothing happened. I blame them—they didn’t follow protocol, and people died. If they’d acted faster, maybe I wouldn’t feel so broken.  

I lose my temper. I’ve snapped at residents, cursed out a supervisor. It’s not like me, but I can’t always stop it.  

And lately… I’ve heard voices—mostly at night. A man’s voice, urgent, saying, “Code not responding.” I know it’s not real, but it feels close, like it’s in the room. I haven’t told anyone. I’m not sure if it’s the stress… or something more. It only happens when I’m exhausted, never at work. I can’t afford to lose control there. I’m fine—mostly. But sleep? I don’t sleep. I survive.
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h011.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been having these strange spells lately—moments where I’m right back in that old house during the fire, like it’s happening all over again. I smell the smoke, I hear my son calling, and I can’t move. It only lasts a minute, maybe, but it feels real. Afterward, I’m shaky, sometimes crying. I don’t go near that part of town anymore. Don’t even like looking at old photos. Too much.

I keep thinking this world isn’t safe—not for anyone. Maybe it never was. I should’ve gotten us out faster. I keep wondering—could I have done more? It was my home. My responsibility.

Sometimes I see my husband sitting in his chair, but when I turn the light on, no one’s there. Once, I heard him say my name. Not just memory—like he was here. I threw a teacup once when someone startled me in the kitchen. Didn’t mean to. Felt like I was defending myself.

I don’t sleep well. Jumpy. Get upset easy. The doctor asked if I hear things, and yes—but only things tied to *that time*. Or at least, I think so. I can’t always tell what’s real anymore.
D018-D005_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h012.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been having a hard time lately—just over the past few months, really. Ever since that incident last year when I was showing a property and things… got out of hand. I don’t like to talk about it, but sometimes even hearing a loud noise, like a door slamming in an empty house, makes my chest tighten and my hands shake. I avoid those kinds of listings now—older homes, quiet neighborhoods. I tell myself it’s just business, but honestly, I can’t stand being alone in a room that feels too still.  

I keep thinking it was my fault. I should’ve left earlier, should’ve brought someone with me. Now I feel like the world isn’t safe anymore—like danger’s always waiting in the shadows. I snap sometimes, too. Last week I threw my phone across the office after a client raised their voice. It scared me more than them.  

And there are times—usually when I’m exhausted—I swear I hear footsteps behind me, or someone whispering my name in an empty room. I turn around, and no one’s there. It’s not like seeing something, exactly. Just… sounds. I don’t know if it’s stress, grief, or something worse. I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h013.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—ever since that night when everything felt like it went dark. I don’t like talking about it, but certain sounds, even a car backfiring, make my chest tighten and my hands shake. I get flashes—not clear images, just feelings, like I’m back there, but not really. I try not to think about it. I avoid talking about it with my wife, even though she asks. 

My job’s slipping. I used to thrive on the pressure, but now I snap at colleagues over small things. Last week I threw a coffee cup across the office. I regret it, but in that moment, it felt like I was defending myself from something… or someone. I keep thinking it’s my fault—like if I’d acted differently, maybe it wouldn’t have happened. 

Sometimes I hear voices—like someone whispering my name when no one’s there. It’s never loud, and I know it’s not real, but it unsettles me. I wonder if the world’s just a trap waiting to catch you. I don’t feel safe anywhere anymore. I don’t know if it’s stress… or something breaking inside.
D018-D005_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h014.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been off since the accident in the kitchen last year—got distracted for a second, and my teammate got burned bad. Since then, his scream just… repeats in my head, outta nowhere. I’ll be plating and suddenly hear it, clear as day. I try not to think about it, but the more I push it down, the worse it gets. Sometimes I snap at the line cooks—yell, curse—especially if someone drops a pan or moves too slow. I know it’s not their fault, but I can’t stop myself.

I keep thinking I should’ve seen it coming. That it was my job to protect them. Now I feel like I can’t trust anyone, not even the crew I’ve worked with for years. The world feels like it’s wired wrong—like danger’s always one misstep away. I don’t talk about it much, not even with my wife.  

And… there are things I see sometimes. Quick flashes—steam turning into smoke, shadows where no one’s standing. I can’t say if it’s stress or if my mind’s breaking. They don’t feel like memories, but they’re not exactly dreams either. I just don’t know what’s real half the time.
D018-D005_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h015.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h016.question:
I’ve been having a lot of trouble keeping things together, especially at work. I’m a sound engineer—used to being sharp with my ears, but now I keep hearing things that aren’t there… like voices whispering during quiet takes, or sudden loud bangs that no one else reacts to. I don’t know if it’s stress or something else.  

It’s been going on for a few months now, but it all kind of started after that incident near the subway last winter—the one where I saw that fight go bad. I can’t get the images out of my head. They just pop up—me seeing the blood, the sound of the scream cutting off… sometimes I’ll be mixing a track and suddenly I’m right back there, heart racing. So I try not to think about it, avoid anything that might trigger it—certain sounds, crowded places.  

Honestly, I blame the cops, like, why weren’t they there when it happened? Someone should’ve stopped it. I’m always watching exits, checking corners, even in the studio. It’s exhausting. The voices? I can’t tell if they’re part of that memory or… something worse. They don’t feel exactly like flashbacks. They just… show up.
D018-D005_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h016.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been having a hard time lately—more than I can explain. It started a few months ago, maybe after that incident at the plant. Nothing officially happened to me, but I was there when the assembly line jammed and the machine… well, it wasn’t pretty. Since then, I can’t seem to shake the feeling that something’s off. I notice noises—sudden movements—and my chest tightens like something’s about to go wrong. I leave through different exits every shift, just in case. I check the doors, the emergency lights, make sure I know where to go. Feels stupid, but if I don’t, my mind races.

I avoid going near that section now. Won’t even walk past it, even if it means going the long way. I keep thinking—what if I had caught it sooner? I was supposed to be watching. I should’ve said something.

And sometimes… I hear voices. Like someone calling my name in the warehouse when no one’s there. Once I could’ve sworn I saw a shadow near the presses. But it’s never there. My wife says I’ve been distant. I tell myself it’s stress. Maybe I’m just… worn down.
D018-D005_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h017.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h018.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—like my mind just throws up images I don’t want to see. Something at work reminded me of the incident, and suddenly I was back there, heart racing, sweat on my palms. It’s been happening more since the anniversary passed, though it’s not like I keep track. I don’t *want* to think about it, so I distract myself—work late, rearrange tasks, anything to stay busy. But even then, it sneaks in.

I can’t help but think about what *they* did—how if certain people hadn’t ignored the red flags, if they’d listened when I raised concerns, none of this would’ve happened. It wasn’t on me. They let it happen.

Most days, I walk into a room and immediately check the exits, notice who’s standing where, if someone seems off. Not that anything’s wrong—but I need to be sure. Lately, though, I’ve woken up confused, like I heard someone call my name in the apartment when no one’s there. It’s only happened a few times. I chalk it up to stress. Or maybe not sleeping right. I can’t tell if it’s connected to the past or just… my mind fraying at the edges.
D018-D005_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h018.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h019.question:
I’ve been off since the accident at the plant last year—something about seeing one of my guys get caught in the line… it rewired something in me, I think. I keep seeing it, outta nowhere—him falling, the noise—just flashes while I’m at dinner or trying to sleep. Doesn’t help that the boss made me testify, like it was my fault. I know they just needed answers, but why pin it all on me? I wasn’t even at that station. 

I don’t go back to that side of the factory. Can’t. I check the exits every time I walk into a room now—gotta know where to go. My wife says I’m jumpy, like I’m watching for something that isn’t there. And sometimes… well, I hear voices—muffled, like through a wall. Can’t make out words. Happens most when I’m alone at night. I don’t know if it’s stress, or guilt, or if my mind’s breaking. But it’s not like I’m seeing things that aren’t there… not exactly. Just… echoes. And I don’t know who to trust anymore—not even my own head.
D018-D005_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h019.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h020.question:
I’ve been struggling for about the past six months—maybe longer, I don’t know. Ever since that night walking home when I was attacked, I can’t seem to quiet my mind. I keep seeing flashes of it—out of nowhere—like a film loop: the hand grabbing my arm, the voice. I try not to think about it, but it pushes through, especially at night when I’m trying to write my thesis. So I avoid anything that reminds me—dark streets, certain sounds, even some people on campus. It’s hard to focus on research when my brain keeps pulling me back.

I should’ve taken a different route. I should’ve been more aware. It’s stupid—I know—but I keep thinking I caused it somehow. Since then, I check the locks on my apartment door three times before bed. I scan every room I enter, always noting where the exits are. It feels like I’m waiting for something to happen again.

And… sometimes, I hear whispers when no one’s there. Not full sentences—just murmurs, like the wind. I can’t tell if it’s my mind replaying the attack or if it’s something else. I haven’t told anyone. What if I can’t trust what I’m hearing? What if I’m losing it?
D018-D005_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h020.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—ever since that night during the audit in the old factory district. I can’t go back to that area; just seeing the building on a map tightens my chest. Sometimes, a sound—like a metal door slamming—sends me into a cold sweat, like I’m right back there. I don’t know what happened exactly, but I remember feeling utterly exposed, like I failed everyone. I carry that shame every day, like I should’ve been stronger.

I don’t feel joy like before. My daughter’s birthday party last month, my wife’s smile—they’re just… distant. Like I’m watching through glass. And I lash out. At work, I cursed at a junior analyst over a minor error. At home, I snapped at my wife for nothing. I don’t mean to, but the anger boils up so fast.

Then there are the voices. Not all the time—only in quiet moments. A whisper saying *“you let them down”* when no one’s there. Once, I saw a shadow near the garage that looked like one of the guards from that night—but when I turned, nothing. I can’t tell if it’s my mind replaying the past… or breaking. I just know I can’t function like this.
D018-D005_h021.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h021.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—night after night—about the incident back when I worked at the courthouse. You remember that case, don’t you? The one with the man in the hallway… I can’t say much, but ever since then, it’s like my mind won’t quiet down. I wake up sweating, heart racing, like I’m back there. It’s not just the dreams, though. I feel on edge all the time, like something’s about to happen. I snap at my wife over little things—once I threw a coffee mug against the wall. I didn’t mean to, but the anger just explodes.

I used to take pride in my work—thirty years of service, commendations, all of it. Now, it means nothing. It’s like I can’t feel proud, or happy, even when the grandkids visit. But here’s what’s strange: sometimes, when I’m alone in the study, I hear a whisper—just a word, like “case” or “dismissed”—but no one’s there. I turn around, and it’s empty. I don’t know if it’s my mind playing tricks, or if it’s tied to the past… I can’t tell what’s real anymore. I don’t feel crazy, but I can’t explain it either. This has been going on for about six months now.
D018-D005_h022.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h022.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—maybe longer, I don’t know. Ever since that night on the train, I can’t seem to shake the feeling that something’s watching me, even in my lab. I work alone a lot, analyzing data late into the night, and sometimes I hear my name whispered, or I catch a shadow moving in the corner of the room. It’s not like I see people, exactly, but the sound feels so close, like someone’s breathing right behind me. 

I get angry—really angry—over small things. Last week I threw a stack of papers across the room during a meeting. I didn’t mean to, but it felt like the frustration had been building forever. I finally published my first sole-author paper, something I’d worked on for years, but I didn’t feel anything. No pride, no joy. Just… empty. 

Certain smells—like cigarette smoke or wet pavement—make my chest tighten. I have to leave the room. And sometimes, when I’m tired, the whispers get louder. I can’t tell if they’re coming from outside or from inside my head. I don’t want to lose my mind, but I also can’t keep pretending this is normal.
D018-D005_h023.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h023.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h024.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for months—like I can’t ever relax. Even small things set me off: a certain sound, a shadow in the corner, something about the way the light hits my screen at night. My chest gets tight, my hands shake. Sometimes I just freeze. I work from home drawing webtoons, and there are days when I can’t even open my tablet because I feel like I’m underwater, like something’s watching.

I’m scared all the time. Not of anything specific—just this constant buzz of fear, like waiting for something bad to happen. I finished a big arc last month, got great feedback, but… I didn’t feel anything. No pride, no joy. Just numb. I used to love this work. Now it feels like going through the motions.

And then there are the episodes. When the panic builds, I sometimes lash out—slam my fist into the wall, throw my pen, once I even shoved a delivery guy when he startled me at the door. I didn’t mean to. I just… snapped.

Sometimes I see things. A figure at the end of the hall. A face in the static of a turned-off monitor. I don’t know if it’s real, or my mind breaking, or if it’s *him* again. I don’t want to say too much—he might be gone, but I still feel him here.
D018-D005_h024.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h024.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h025.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—where I’m back on a flight during that emergency landing. I can hear the alarms, feel the plane drop, people screaming. I wake up gasping, drenched in sweat, heart pounding like I’m still up there. It’s been happening for months now. Even when I’m not flying, I feel on edge, like something’s about to go wrong. I can’t relax, not really. My husband says I jump at nothing. 

Work is harder than it should be. I got praised last month for handling a difficult passenger, but it didn’t feel like an achievement—just something I had to get through. I don’t feel proud of much anymore. Some days, I get so tense it spills over. Once, I threw a cup across the galley because a colleague startled me. It scared me more than them, honestly.

And… sometimes, when I’m exhausted, I think I hear a voice—like a whisper in the cabin when no one’s there. Or I catch a shape in the corner of my eye. But when I turn, it’s nothing. I don’t know if it’s the stress, the dreams, lack of sleep… I just know it’s getting harder to tell what’s real when I’m running on three hours between flights.
D018-D005_h025.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h025.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia
